name: Flaming Katy
description: A succulent flowering plant from Madagascar, Flaming Katy produces dense clusters of small, colorful four-petaled flowers in vibrant reds, pinks, oranges, yellows, or white that can last 6-8 weeks. The flowers sit atop thick, glossy, scalloped leaves that store water, making this plant remarkably drought-tolerant and forgiving of occasional neglect. Growing 6-12 inches tall, it's a popular gift plant during holidays due to its long-lasting blooms and easy care requirements. As a succulent, it needs less water than typical flowering plants and thrives on benign neglect. With proper rest periods and bright light, kalanchoe can be encouraged to rebloom year after year, providing colorful displays multiple times annually.
toxicity: Toxic to cats and dogs. Can cause vomiting and diarrhea, and rarely an abnormal heart rhythm.
careInstructions: Water thoroughly only when soil is completely dry - typically every 10-14 days
Give it 6-8 hours of bright light daily - some direct sun is fine, but shade it from hot afternoon sun
Remove spent flower clusters by cutting stem at base
After flowering, cut back stems by half to encourage bushiness
To trigger reblooming: give it 14 hours of complete darkness each night for at least 6 weeks in fall or winter
Fertilize monthly during active growth with a balanced or higher-phosphorus fertilizer; feed less while triggering blooms
Keep it around 70°F by day and 60°F at night while triggering blooms - too cold or too hot can stop flowering
commonProblems: No flowers after first bloom: Needs darkness treatment (12-14 hours for 6 weeks)
Root rot: Overwatering - this is a succulent that prefers dry conditions
Leggy growth after blooming: Normal - prune back by half to restore shape
Yellowing leaves: Overwatering most likely, or natural aging
Short bloom period: Natural, but cooler temps (60-65°F) extend flowering

fertilizing.tip: Fertilize monthly during active growth with a balanced or higher-phosphorus fertilizer; feed less while triggering blooms

whatsNormal: If it won't rebloom, it isn't getting long enough dark nights — even room lights can interrupt them.
Blooms about four months after its six weeks of long nights, and the flowers last for weeks.
Tiny plantlets sometimes form along the leaf edges — they can be potted up.

propagation.tip: Root stem or leaf cuttings, or pot up plantlets from the leaf edges.

flags.note: Toxicity: NC State says K. blossfeldiana is toxic to children, dogs and cats; symptoms come from ASPCA's Kalanchoe entry. Horses aren't rated.
Monthly fertilizing is from the original catalog; MOBOT only specifies the fertilizer type.
Winter watering interval (14 days) is our estimate — the sources only say to reduce watering from fall to late winter.
Changed: bloom trigger 12-14 → 14 hours of darkness, at 70°F days / 60°F nights (both sources); light now "Bright Indirect to Direct" with afternoon shade (NC State).
